physics_goals.quote: A search for muon anti-neutrino to electron anti-neutrino oscillations was conducted by the Liquid Scintillator Neutrino Detector at the Los Alamos Neutron Science Center using muon anti-neutrinos from positive muon decay at rest.
physics_goals.value: Search for muon-antineutrino to electron-antineutrino oscillations from muon decay at rest

summary.plain: A tank of mineral oil at Los Alamos National Laboratory, New Mexico, that watched for neutrinos changing type just 30 metres from where an accelerator beam produced them. From 1993 to 1998 it reported more electron-antineutrinos than expected, a puzzling result that later experiments tried to confirm or rule out.
summary.technical: 167 t mineral-oil/scintillator (Cherenkov + scintillation) detector at LAMPF/LANSCE, Los Alamos, 30 m from the A6 beam-stop neutrino source, using an 800 MeV proton beam. Took data 1993-1998 and reported a statistically significant excess of ν̄e candidate events consistent with ν̄μ → ν̄e oscillation at short baseline, a result in tension with standard three-flavour oscillation and a long-standing driver of sterile-neutrino searches.
